title: How Buy Now Pay Later is Preying on Gen Z
summary: Gen Z commentary channel argues BNPL has spread from big-ticket items to groceries and festival tickets, preying on financially stressed young adults.

assertions.quote: Americans are using more and more of the buy now, pay later method when they're buying their groceries
the average purchase price per order goes up drastically if a purchase is made using a buy now pay later
They target shoppers whose prefrontal cortexes aren't developed yet.

verdicts.note: Confirmed by CFPB, TransUnion, and multiple survey-based studies of the BNPL user base.

FEDS Notes table 3: BNPL use is highest among younger adults with lower credit scores (e.g. 31% for ages 18-29 with scores under 620) and lowest among older adults with high scores (6% for 60+ with scores above 720), showing age and credit history both independently predict use.

assertions.quote: the desire for instant experience has overtaken the discipline of just saving up and paying cash

verdicts.note: Consistent with survey data (e.g., LendingTree) finding most users report buying more than they would have paying in full.
NBER: making BNPL available increased conversions by 9 percentage points (13% relative), meaning a meaningful share of buyers purchased who would not have converted otherwise.

Same CFPB passage: the lenders' own conversion-lift and AOV-increase marketing metrics lead CFPB to conclude many BNPL consumers 'may not simply be shifting their existing purchases to a new payment platform; they may be spending (and borrowing) more than they otherwise would.'

assertions.quote: there's so many of them and it's super easy to lose track what exactly you should be paying for
